summary: The City of Toronto's most visible war memorial is the Cenotaph at Old City Hall. It is the site of annual Remembrance Day ceremonies as Canadian veterans of every major conflict since World War One are recognized on the memorial. However, Afghanistan has not been added to the monument. The City of Toronto has recognized veterans of the Afghanistan war. The City recently accepted the donation of a decommissioned LAVIII, installed in front of the Fort York Armoury on City lands leased to the federal Department of National Defence in recognition of the sacrifice of veterans of the Afghanistan conflict. Given the central location of the Cenotaph at Old City Hall, and its function during Remembrance Day ceremonies, it is appropriate to consider adding "AFGHANISTAN" to the monument to recognize the contributions of Canadian soldiers in the nation's most recent major war, while respecting the design and heritage of the existing memorial.
decided: City Council on July 23, 24, 25, 26, 27 and 30, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council direct the General Manager, Economic Development and Culture, and the City Clerk to examine the impact of adding the word "AFGHANISTAN" to the Cenotaph at Old City Hall, on the heritage, design, and function of the memorial.

motions.desc: Majority required - MM44.18 - Adopt the item
